decision: Fix git-control-tower review polling to pin the resolved API base for the lifetime of a review run. Proposed implementation: after the initial POST /review/run succeeds, capture the resolved base or require pollJob to use the same API base options that succeeded for the start request, so transient failures in DetectPortFromVrooli cannot make later status polls fail with an empty API base. Also print or preserve the job id before waiting so operators can recover status after a poll failure. Add a regression test that simulates a base resolver returning a valid base for the start request and empty on a later poll; review run should either continue using the pinned base or emit the job id with recovery guidance instead of losing the run.
rationale: Bug inbox knw-1778774971484367104 reported three GCT review runs that started and polled progress, then failed with 'polling job status: api base URL is empty', while explicit --api-base summary calls succeeded against http://localhost:18710. Scientific-debugging investigation found no prior fix recurrence. Code evidence: review run starts the job in scenarios/git-control-tower/cli/domains/review/register.go:80 and polls through pollJob at lines 97-111; every poll calls core.Get, which reaches packages/cli-core/cliapp/scenario_app.go:457-470 and packages/cli-core/cliutil/apiclient.go:26-36, reapplying APIBaseOptions on each request. API base resolution invokes DetectPortFromVrooli via packages/cli-core/cliapp/scenario_app.go:194-201 and :230-231, whose detector returns empty on any command failure per packages/cli-core/cliutil/port_detector.go:27-31. This explains a mid-run failure despite the API remaining reachable: the status poll re-resolves the base instead of reusing the base that already started the job. Direct patching is forbidden for bug-investigator, so this decision is the smallest durable action.

decision: Fix GCT review runs to use a single dependency-availability snapshot for each run and preserve dependency execution errors instead of reporting failed tests with zero counts.
rationale: Bug inbox knw-1778796308148709144 reported GCT review output where tests were failed/skipped inconsistently and phase-level test evidence collapsed to total=0. Scientific-debugging reproduced the current failure with 'git-control-tower review run landing-page-business-suite --checks=tests --details=5 --json': job da12afc9-aacb-4470-8a2a-9dc91bfbca2d returned status=failed, checks.tests=failed, error='all checks failed or were skipped'. GCT runtime logs for the same job show the check failed because BaseClient could not resolve test-genie: 'resolve test-genie url: api-core discovery command_failed ... no running runtime ports found'. In the same window, 'git-control-tower review summary landing-page-business-suite --json' returned capabilities.test-genie=true and dimensions.tests available=true total=0. Code evidence: scenarios/git-control-tower/api/main.go creates CapabilityRegistry with a 30s TTL; review_handler.go dispatchCheck uses capabilities.IsAvailable before ExecuteSuite, but TestGenieClient.ExecuteSuite re-resolves the service URL through httpclient.go BaseClient.resolveBaseURL. review_handler_dimensions.go fetchTestsDimension also returns &TestsDimension{Available:true} with zero counts when ListExecutions errors or returns no rows, erasing the infrastructure failure. Proposed fix: for each review run, snapshot dependency availability and resolved base URLs or make client calls consume the same successful resolution used by the capability check; when a dependency cannot be resolved or ListExecutions fails, expose a skipped/infrastructure status with the error rather than available=true/total=0; add regression tests for stale capability cache plus client-resolution failure and for ListExecutions error semantics.
